'''Figgie 'obbin''', also called '''figgie hobbin''', is an old Cornish recipe. It is good served hot with [[Cookbook:Clotted Cream|clotted cream]], burnt cream, or [[Cookbook:Custard|baked custard]]; or cold with tea or coffee or cocoa.

==Ingredients==

* 2 parts by weight of [[Cookbook:Flour|self raising flour]] (or [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|plain flour]] plus [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]])
* 2 parts by weight of [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (and/or [[Cookbook:Sultanas|sultanas]] if desired)
* 1 part by weight (i.e. half the weight of the flour in total) of a 50/50 mix of [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]] and other [[Cookbook:Fat|fat]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] or [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

==Procedure==

# Rub the [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]], fat, and flour together.
# Mix in the raisins, and add enough water or milk to make a stiff [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] to about 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick. Press gently into a prepared shallow baking tin or dish.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|hot oven]] for about 35–45 minutes.
== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Currants and/or sultanas may be mixed with or substituted for raisins.
* Vegetable suet, vegetable lard, or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], can be used instead of [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Mutton|mutton]] [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]] and [[Cookbook:Dripping|dripping]]; this will give a lighter cake.
* Figgie/Fig/Figs are Cornish dialect words pertaining to raisins
* From ''Perranporth W.I.'' in ''Cornish Recipes, Ancient & Modern, 22nd Edition, The Cornwall Federation of Women's Institutes 1965.'' First collected & published by Edith Martin, Tregavethan, Truro, 1929, for The Cornwall F. of W. I.
